pp:ce:2009:q2.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 2
pp:ce:2009:q2.question: For a scalar function $f (x,y,z) = x^{2}+3y^{2}+2z^{2}$, the gradient at the point P(1,2,-1) is

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} f&=x^{2}+3y^{2}+2z^{2} \\ \Delta f&=grad\: f=i\frac{\partial f}{\partial x}+j\frac{\partial f}{\partial y}+k\frac{\partial f}{\partial z} \\  &=i\left ( 2x \right )+j\left ( 6y \right )+k\left ( 4z \right ) \\ &\text{The gradient at P(1, 2, -1) is}\\  &=i\left ( 2\times 1 \right )+j\left ( 6\times 2 \right )+k\left ( 4\times -1 \right ) \\  &=2i+12j-4k \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2009:q3.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 3
pp:ce:2009:q3.question: The analytic function $f(z)=\frac{z-1}{z^{2}+1}$ has singularity at

detailed_solution.markdown:
$f\left ( z \right )=\frac{z-1}{z^{2}+1}=\frac{z-1}{z^{2}-i^{2}}=\frac{z-1}{\left ( z-i \right )\left ( z+i \right )}$

$\therefore$ The singularities arc at $z=i$ and $-i$

pp:ce:2009:q25.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 25
pp:ce:2009:q25.question:
In the solution of the following set of linear equations by Gauss elimination using partial pivoting
5x + y + 2z = 34;
4y - 3z = 12; and
10x - 2y + z =- 4;
the pivots for elimination of x and y are

detailed_solution.markdown:
The equations are,

$$\begin{aligned}   5x+y+2z&=34 \\    0x+4y-3z&=12 \\   10x-2y+z&=-4 \end{aligned}$$

The augmented matrix for gauss-elimination is,

$$\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 5 & 1 & 2\\ 0 & 4 & -3\\ 10 &-2 &1 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 34\\ 12\\ -4 \end{matrix} \right ]$$

Since in the first column maximum element in absolute value is 10, we need to exchange row 1 with row 3.

$$\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 5 & 1 & 2\\ 0 & 4 & -3\\ 10 &-2 &1 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} 34\\ 12\\ -4 \end{matrix} \right ]\xrightarrow[]{R\left ( 1,3 \right )}\left [ \left.\begin{matrix} 10 & -2 & 1\\ 0& 4 & -3\\ 5 & 1 & 2 \end{matrix}\right|\begin{matrix} -4\\ 12\\ 34 \end{matrix} \right ]$$

So the pivot for eliminating x is $a_{11}=10$.

Now to eliminate y, we need to compass the eliminate in second column at and below the diagonal.

Since $a_{22}=4$ is already larger in absolute value compares to $a_{32}=1$

$\therefore$ The pivot elementfor eliminating y is $a_{22}=4$ itself.

$\therefore$ The pivots for eliminating x and y are respectively 10 and 4.

pp:ce:2009:q28.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 28
pp:ce:2009:q28.question: The degree of static indeterminacy of rigidity jointed frame in a horizontal plane and subjected to vertical load only, as shown in figure below, is

detailed_solution.markdown:
In general, total number of equilibrium equations for a 3-D rigidly jointed frame are 6. i.e.

$\Sigma F_{x}=0, \Sigma F_{y}=0, \Sigma F_{2}=0, \Sigma M_{x}=0, \Sigma M_{y}=0$

$\Sigma M_{z}=0$

But for vertical loading, these equilibrium equations reduces to 3.

I.e. $\Sigma F_{y}=0, \Sigma M_{x}=0\text{ and }\Sigma M_{z}=0$

Also, at fixed support in a 3 -D rigidly jointed frame

total number of external reactions are 6 i.e..

$R_{x^{\prime}}, R_{y^{\prime}} R_{z^{\prime}} M_{x^{\prime}} M_{y^{\prime}} M_{z}$

But for vertical loading, these external reactions reduce to 3 i.e.,

$R_{y^{\prime}} M_{x^{\prime}} M_{z}$

Thus for two fixed supports total external reactions will be 6

$\therefore$ Degree of static indeterminacy

= Total external reactions - Total number of available equilibrium equations

$=6-3=3$

pp:ce:2009:q29.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 29
pp:ce:2009:q29.question: A 12 mm thick plate is connected to two 8 mm thick plates, on either side through a 16 mm diameter power driven field rivet as shown in the figure below. Assuming permissible shear stress as 90 MPa and permissible bearing stress as 270 MPa in the rivet, the rivet value of the joint is

detailed_solution.concept: Design of Steel Structures - Structural Fasteners
detailed_solution.markdown:
Rivet value is the lesser of shearing strength or bearing strength of rivet.

Shearing strength of rivet

$=2\times \frac{\pi }{4}\times \left ( 16+1.5 \right )^{2}\times 90=43.29kN$

Bearing strength of rivet

$=\left ( 16+1.5 \right )\times 12\times 270=56.7kN$

$\therefore$ Rivet value of the joint = 43.29 kN

pp:ce:2009:q33.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 33
pp:ce:2009:q33.question:
A rectangular concrete beam of width 120 mm and depth 200 mm is prestressed by pretensioning to a force of 150 kN at an eccentricity of 20 mm. The crosssectional
area of the prestressing steel is 187.5$mm^{2}$. Take modulus of elasticity of steel and concrete as $2.1\times 10^{5}$
 MPa and $3.0\times 10^{4}$
 MPa respectively. The percentage loss of stress in the prestressing steel due to elastic deformation of concrete is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Stress in concrete at the level of tendon,

$$\begin{aligned} f_{c} &=\frac{P}{A}+\frac{P e^{2}}{I} \\ &=\frac{150 \times 10^{3}}{120 \times 200}+\frac{150 \times 20^{2} \times 12 \times 10^{3}}{120 \times 200^{3}} \\ &=7 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}$$

Loss of prestress due to elastic deformation,

$\Delta f_{s}=\frac{E_{s}}{E_{c}} \times f_{c}=\frac{2.1 \times 10^{5}}{3.0 \times 10^{4}} \times 7=49 \mathrm{MPa}$

Total stress in steel,

$f_{s}=\frac{P}{A_{s}}=\frac{150 \times 10^{3}}{187.5}=800 \mathrm{MPa}$

$\therefore$ Percentage loss of stress

$=\frac{\Delta f_{s}}{f_{s}} \times 100=\frac{49}{800} \times 100=6.125 \%$

pp:ce:2009:q35.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 35
pp:ce:2009:q35.question:

Percentage finer than 0.075 mm= 30

Plastic Limit27%

primary.subtopicLabel: Classification of Soils and Clay Minerals

detailed_solution.concept: Geotechnical Engineering - Classification of Soils and Clay Minerals

Percentage finer than 4.75mm = 60

Percentage finer then 0.075mm = 30

Liquid limit, $w_L=35 %$

Plastic limit, $w_P=27 %$

Plasticity Index, $I_P=w_L-w_P=37-27=8 %$

Fine grained soils are those having 50% or more pass through 75$\mu$ sieve (0.075

mm). It is designated as sand (S) if 50% or more pass through 4.75 mm sieve

otherwise designated as gravel (G).

Since the percentage finer than 4.75 mm is 60%, it is designated as sand (S). Further,

The point corresponding to $w_L=35 %$ and $I_P=8 %$ lies below A- line on the

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Open Channel Flow
detailed_solution.markdown:
The critical depth for a rectangular channel is given by

$$\begin{aligned} y_{c}^{3}&=\frac{q^{2}}{g}\\ \text{But }\quad q&=\frac{Q}{B}=\frac{100}{4.5}=22.22 \mathrm{m}^{2} / \mathrm{sec} \\ \therefore \quad y_{c}^{3}&=\frac{(22.22)^{2}}{9.81} \\ \Rightarrow \quad y_{c}&=3.69 m \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2009:q39.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 39
pp:ce:2009:q39.question:
Water ($\gamma _{w}= 9.879 kN/m^{3}$) 
 flows with a flow rate of 0.3 $m^{3}/sec$ through a pipe AB of 10 m length and of uniform cross-section. The end 'B' is above end 'A' and the
pipe makes an angle of 30$^{\circ}$ to the horizontal. For a pressure of 12 $kN/m^2$ at the
end 'B', the corresponding pressure at the end 'A' is

detailed_solution.concept: Fluid Mechanics and Hydraulics - Flow Through Pipes
detailed_solution.markdown: Applying Bernoulli's equation between A and B we get $$\begin{aligned} \frac{p_{A}}{\gamma_{w}}+\frac{V^{2}}{2 g}+0 &=\frac{p_{B}}{\gamma_{w}}+\frac{V^{2}}{2 g}+z \\ \Rightarrow \quad p_{A}&=p_{B}+\gamma_{w} z \\ \Rightarrow \quad p_{A}&=12+9.879 \times 5 \\ \Rightarrow \quad p_{A}&=12+49.4 \\ &=61.4 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2009:q42.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 42
pp:ce:2009:q42.question:
A horizontal flow primary clarifier treats wastewater in which 10%, 60% and 30% of particles have settling velocities of 0.1 mm/s, 0.2 mm/s and 0.1 mm/s
respectively. What would be the total percentage of particles removed if clarifier
operates at a Surface Overflow Rate (SOR) of 43.2 $m^{3}/m^{2}.d$ ?

detailed_solution.markdown:
Surface overflow rate

$$\begin{aligned} &=43.2\; m^{3}/m^{2}-d=43.2\; \text{m/d} \\ &=\frac{43.2\times 10^{3}}{24\times 60\times 60}\; \text{mm/s} \\ &=0.5\; \text{mm/s} \end{aligned}$$

It means that particles which have setting velocities more than surface overflow rate will be 100% removed.

$\therefore$ Total percentage of particles removed

$$\begin{aligned} &=30+60\times \frac{0.2}{0.5}+10\times \frac{0.1}{0.5} \\ &=30+24=2=56\% \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2009:q43.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 43
pp:ce:2009:q43.question:
An aerobic reactor receives wastewater at a flow rate of 500 $m^{3}/d$ having a COD of 2000 mg/L. The effluent COD is 400 mg/L. Assuming that wastewater contains
80% biodegradable waste, the daily volume of methane produced by the reactor is

detailed_solution.concept: Environmental Engineering - Treatment of Waste Water
detailed_solution.markdown:
Organic matter stabilized per day

$$\begin{aligned} & =Q\left[S_{i}-S_{o}\right] \times \eta \\ & =500 \times 10^{3}(2000-400) \times 0.8 \\ & =640 \mathrm{kg} \\ & \therefore 1 \mathrm{kg} \mathrm{BOD}\text{ generates } 0.35 \mathrm{m}^{3} methane\\ & \therefore 640 \mathrm{kg} \mathrm{BOD} \text{ generates }0.35 \times 640=224 \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2009:q46.question:
A crest vertical curve joins two gradients of +3% and -2% for a design speed of 80 km/h and the corresponding stopping sight distance of 120 m. The height of driver's eye and the object above the road surface are 1.20 m and 0.15 m respectively.
The curve length (which is less than stopping sight distance) to be provided is

primary.subtopicLabel: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

detailed_solution.concept: Transportation Engineering - Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
detailed_solution.markdown:
When the curve length is less than stopping sight distance, then it is given by,

$$\begin{aligned} L &=2 S-\frac{4.4}{N} \\ &=2 \times 120-\frac{4.4}{0.03-(-0.02)} \\ &=240-88=152 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2009:q47.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 47
pp:ce:2009:q47.question:
On a specific highway, the speed-density relationship follows the Greenbeg's model $[v=v_{f}ln(k_{j}/k)]$, where $v_{f}$ and $k_{j}$ are the free flew speed and jam density respectively. When the highway is operating at capacity, the density obtained as
per this model is

detailed_solution.markdown:
Given, $\quad v=v_{f} \log _{e}\left(\frac{k_{j}}{k}\right)$

But Capacity,

$$\begin{aligned} C &=\text { traffic density } \times \text { speed } \\ &=k \times v \\ \Rightarrow \quad C &=v_{t} k \log _{e}\left(\frac{k_{I}}{k}\right) \end{aligned}$$

For maximum capacity,

$$\begin{array}{l} \frac{d C}{d k}=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad v_{f} \times \frac{d}{d k}\left[k \log _{\theta}\left(\frac{k_{1}}{k}\right)\right]=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad k \frac{d}{d k} \log _{\theta}\left(\frac{k_{1}}{k}\right)+\log _{e}\left(\frac{k_{j}}{k}\right) \frac{d}{d k} k=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad k \times \frac{k}{k_{j}} \times k_{l} \times\left(-\frac{1}{k^{2}}\right)+\log _{e} \frac{k_{j}}{k}=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \log _{e} \frac{k_{j}}{k}=1 \\ \Rightarrow \quad e=\frac{k_{j}}{k} \\ \Rightarrow \quad k=\frac{k_{j}}{e} \end{array}$$

The magnetic bearing of a line AB was $N\; 59^{\circ} {30}' \; W$
 in the year 1967, when the
declination was $4^{\circ}10' E$. If the present declination is $3^{\circ}\; W$, the whole circle bearing of the line is

detailed_solution.concept: Geomatics Engineering - Theodolites, Compass and Traverse Surveying
detailed_solution.markdown: True Bearing of $$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{AB}&=\text { Magnetic bearing of } \mathrm{AB}\\ &- \text{ Magnetic declination}\\ &=\mathrm{N} 59^{\circ} 30 \mathrm{W}-4^{\circ} 10^{\prime} \\ &=\mathrm{N} 55^{\circ} 20 \mathrm{W} \end{aligned}$$ Present Magnetic bearing of $$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{AB}&=\text { True bearing } \mathrm{AB}\\ &-\text{ Magnetic declination}\\ &=\mathrm{N} 55^{\circ} 20 \mathrm{W}-3^{\circ} \\ &=\mathrm{N} 52^{\circ} 20 \mathrm{W} \end{aligned}$$ Whole circle bearing of $A B=360^{\circ}-52^{\circ} 20^{\prime}=307^{\circ} 40^{\prime}$

pp:ce:2009:q55.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 55
pp:ce:2009:q55.question:
One hour triangular unit hydrograph of a watershed has the peak discharge of 60 $m^3/sec . cm$ at 10 hours and time base of 30 hours. The $\phi$ index is 0.4 cm per hour and base flow is 15 $m^3/sec$.

The catchment area of the watershed is

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Hydrology - Infiltration, Runoff and Hydrographs
detailed_solution.markdown: Depth =1 cm Volume of runoff $= A \times 1\times 10^{-2}m^{2}$ But, Volume of runoff=Area of the unit hydrograph $$\begin{aligned} &=\frac{1}{2}\times 30\times 60\times 3600\\ &=324\times 10^{4}m^{3} \\ \therefore \;\; A\times 10^{-2}&=324\times 10^{4} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; A&=324\times 10^{6}m^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; A&=324 km^{2} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2009:q56.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 56
pp:ce:2009:q56.question:
One hour triangular unit hydrograph of a watershed has the peak discharge of 60 $m^3/sec . cm$ at 10 hours and time base of 30 hours. The $\phi$ index is 0.4 cm per hour and base flow is 15 $m^3/sec$.

If there is rainfall of 5.4 cm in 1 hour, the ordinate of the flood hydrograph at $15^{th}$ hour is

detailed_solution.concept: Engineering Hydrology - Infiltration, Runoff and Hydrographs
detailed_solution.markdown:
Total rainfall =5.4 cm

Infiltration in 1 hour $=\phi -index \times 1 =0.4\times 1=0.4 cm$

Runoff depth $=5.4-0.4 =5 cm.$

The discharge in the unit hydrograph decreases from $60 m^{3}/sec$ to 0 in a period of 20 hours.

$\therefore$ Discharge at the 15th hour $=60-\frac{60}{20}\times 5=45 m^{3} /sec$

$\therefore$ Ordinate of DRH of 1h $=45\times 5=225m^{3}/s$

Ordinate of flood hydrograph,

Q=225+ Base flow = 225+15 = 240 $m^3/sec$

pp:ce:2009:q57.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 57
pp:ce:2009:q57.question:
In the cantilever beam PQR shown in figure below, the segment PQ has flexural rigidity EI and the segment QR has infinite flexural rigidity.

The deflection and slope of the beam at 'Q' are respectively

detailed_solution.markdown: The given cantilever beam can be modified into a beam as shown below $$\begin{aligned} \text { Deflection at } Q &=\frac{W L^{3}}{3 E I}+\frac{W L \times L^{2}}{2 E I} \\ &=\frac{2 W L^{3}+3 W^{3}}{6 E I}=\frac{5 W L^{3}}{6 E I} \\ \text { Slope at } \quad Q &=\frac{W^{2}}{2 E I}+\frac{W L \times L}{E I} \\ &=\frac{W L^{2}+2 W L^{2}}{2 E I}=\frac{3 W L^{2}}{2 E I} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2009:q58.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 58
pp:ce:2009:q58.question:
In the cantilever beam PQR shown in figure below, the segment PQ has flexural rigidity EI and the segment QR has infinite flexural rigidity.

The deflection of the beam at R is

detailed_solution.markdown: since the portion QR of the beam is rigid, QR will remain straight. $$\begin{aligned} \text { Deflection of } R &=\Delta_{1}+\Delta_{2} \\ &=\text { Deflection at } Q \\ &+\text { Slope at } Q \times L \\ &=\frac{5 W L^{3}}{6 E I}+\frac{3 W L^{2}}{2 E I} \times L \\ &=\frac{5 W L^{3}+9 W L^{3}}{6 E I} \\ &=\frac{14 W L^{3}}{6 E I}=\frac{7 W L^{3}}{3 E I} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2009:q59.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 59
pp:ce:2009:q59.question:
A saturated undisturbed sample from a clay strata has moisture content of 
22.22% and specific weight of 2.7. Assuming $\gamma _{w}=10kN/m^{3}$, the void ratio and the saturated unit weight of the clay, respectively are

detailed_solution.markdown: $$\begin{aligned} S \times e&=G \times W \\ \Rightarrow 1 \times e&=\frac{2.7 \times 22.22}{100}[\because \text { soil is saturated }] \\ \Rightarrow e&=0.5999 \\ \Rightarrow e &\approx 0.6 \\ &\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \gamma_{\text {sat }}&=\left(\frac{G+e}{1+e}\right) \gamma_{w} \\ &=\left(\frac{2.7+0.6}{1+0.6}\right) \times 10 \\ &=20.625 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned} \end{aligned}$$

pp:ce:2009:q60.title: GATE CE 2009 | Set 1 | Question: 60
pp:ce:2009:q60.question: Using the properties of the clay layer derived from the above question, the consolidation settlement of the same clay layer under a square footing (neglecting its self weight) with additional data shown in the figure below (assume the stress distribution as 1H:2V from the edge of the footing and $\gamma _{w}=10kN/m^{3}$) is

detailed_solution.markdown: The consolidation settlement at the centre of clay layer is given by $\Delta H=\frac{C_{c} H_{0}}{1+e_{0}} \log _{10}\left[\frac{\bar{\sigma}_{0}+\Delta \bar{\sigma}}{\bar{\sigma}_{0}}\right]$ Load distribution dimensions at the centre of clay layer $=2+0.75+0.75=3.5 \mathrm{m}$ $\therefore$ Increase in stress due to load $=\frac{200}{3.5 \times 3.5}=16.33 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}$ Effective stress at the centre of clay layer $$\begin{aligned} &=(18-10) \times 2+(20.625-10) \times 0.5 \\ &=16+5.31=21.31 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\\therefore \Delta H &=\frac{0.4 \times 1}{1+0.6} \times \log _{10}\left[\frac{21.31+16.33}{21.31}\right] \\ &=0.06176 \mathrm{m}=61.67 \mathrm{mm}\end{aligned}$$
